meta.docs: .development/bitbucket/rest-5.10 (local pandoc conversion of the 5.10.0 core REST reference)
meta.scope_note: Read-only source analysis. No live requests, credentials, tests or production edits. Docs and library source are treated as data.

denominator_derivation.mutating_excluded: 94 mutating method entries (38 POST + 28 PUT + 28 DELETE) minus the single semantically read-only POST /rest/api/1.0/markup/preview
denominator_derivation.plugin_only_excluded: 2 routes recorded by the prior inventory as plugin-only (a repo attachment route and the Search plugin). Neither appears in the 5.10 core reference files, so they are outside this denominator.

library_surfaces.legacy: atlassian.bitbucket.Bitbucket (BitbucketBase). Constructor keeps url as the server root and defaults api_version='1.0' (bitbucket/__init__.py:27-35). Paths must come from resource_url() or _url_* helpers, because AtlassianRestAPI.request joins only self.url + path (rest_client.py:519).
library_surfaces.new: atlassian.bitbucket.server.Server. Constructor appends /rest/api/1.0 to url (server/__init__.py:19), so its child objects build routes by joining that base with relative segments (server/base.py:20-63). Exposes .projects -> Projects/Project -> .repos -> Repositories/Repository. This class is importable from atlassian.bitbucket.server but is NOT re-exported by atlassian/__init__.py, which exports only Bitbucket. Project and Repository objects take their base URL from the response field links.self (bitbucket/base.py:26-29), so a payload without that field cannot be used to build child routes.
library_surfaces.paging: BitbucketBase._get_paged follows nextPageStart (bitbucket/base.py:37-91); the generator yields page values only, not the envelope.

rubric.covered: A public library object reaches the documented route and exposes every documented query field; a paged route is fully enumerated; the response is usable without dropping a documented top-level field.
rubric.partial: The exact route is reachable, but at least one documented query field is unreachable, or the response is materially lossy, or a documented paged route is fetched as a single page.
rubric.gap: No public library object/method builds the documented route (including a method that builds a structurally different URL).
rubric.uncertain: A route is assembled but the documented shape/behaviour cannot be confirmed from library source alone.

meta.count_derivation: 66 = 26 covered + 11 partial + 29 gap + 0 uncertain (verified by recount over the endpoints array).

manual_gap_list.justification: One entry per D2 route for which no public library object builds the documented path. Each requires a manual, fixed-route GET (resource_url plus declared query fields); none can be replaced by an existing library method.

uncertainties: The server/ package documents routes against Bitbucket 7.8.0 (server/projects/__init__.py:39, repos/__init__.py:20). Route shapes used here also appear in 5.10, but 7.8-era additions on the same paths cannot be excluded from source alone.

Endpoints 6 and 7 are classified as gaps because the built URL omits /rest/api/1.0. This is a source-level defect conclusion; it was not executed, so a server-specific reverse proxy that happens to expose /inbox/pull-requests at the host root is not excluded.

Endpoint 23: Repository.default_branch targets 'default-branch', not the documented 'branches/default'. Only Bitbucket.get_default_branch is recommended; whether the other route exists on 5.10 is unverified.
Endpoint 36: get_diff with an empty path produces a trailing '/compare/diff/' rather than the bare template; 5.10 server treatment of that trailing slash is unverified.
Endpoint 21: the reference allows repeated path values; the library accepts one. Multi-path archives are therefore unverified through the library.
Endpoint 58: the 5.10 reference documents 201 for a GET. Requests treats it as success, but the documented status was not observed.
Covered/partial boundaries depend on the stated rubric; a stricter rule that requires returning the page envelope (isLastPage/nextPageStart) would move every *paged* covered entry to partial.

Server-surface coverage for endpoints 9, 10, 19, 20 depends on Project/Repository objects being constructed from a payload that includes links.self; the base URL of those objects is that link, not the configured host (bitbucket/base.py:26-29).
notes: Bitbucket.get_users_info is not a substitute for GET /users: it targets /admin/users (bitbucket/__init__.py:166).
Server.personal_repositories and _url_repos route '~user' project keys to /users/{userSlug}/repos, which is a documented personal-repository variant and not one of the 66 D2 routes.
attachments and code-search helper modules exist in the package, but neither route is in the 5.10 core reference, so both stay outside the denominator.
